Ichampalli and Polavaram irrigation projects 
*382. DR. C. NARAYANA REDDY:  Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have received any request from the 
Government of Andhra Pradesh to execute major irrigation projects such 
as Ichampalli and Polavaram; 
(b) if so, whether Government propose to take them up for execution; 
and 
(c) by when they are likely to be completed? 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RE SOURCES (SHRI ARJUN CHARAN 
SETHI): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
1 
 

RAJYA SABHA [19 August, 2003] 
Statement 
(a) to (c) Yes, sir. The Hon'ble Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 
January, 2001 had requested the Central Government for declaring 
Inchampalli and Pollavaram Projects as National Projects and their 
implementation by the Union Government. After examining the request, 
the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh was informed in February, 
2001 that there was no proposal to treat any such river valley project in 
the country as a National Project. 
Irrigation being a State subject, the responsibility of planning, 
investigation, funding along with priority execution, operation and 
maintenance of irrigation projects, including irrigation and flood control 
Projects primarily rests with the con cerned State Government themselves. 
Inchampalli and Pollavaram Projects involve inter-State aspects and their 
completion depend upon the resolution of inter-State issues between the 
riparian States. 
DR. C. NARAYANA REDDY: Sir, the hon. Minister has, in his reply, 
stated that Ichamapalli and Polavaram projects in Andhra Pradesh cannot 
be taken up as National Projects as ' Irrigation' is a Stat e Subject., Sir, I 
would like to know why the Government of India couldn't declare Ichampalli 
and Polavaram Projects as National Projects when the Damodar Valley 
Project, catering only to the State of West Bengal, had been declared as 
a National Project. 
SHRI ARJUN CHARAN SETHI: Sir, the first step in the implementation 
of such a project is its clearance by the Central Water Commission; then, 
there has to be the investment clearance. There are so many processes 
involved before any project is taken up for implementation. Ichampalli 
and Polavaram projects are inter-State  projects. Unless all the States 
involved in the case of Polavaram project, the States of Orissa, Andhra 
Pradesh and Chhattisgarh and, in the case of Ichampalli project, the States 
of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh - agree on the 
implementation of these projects, these projects cannot be taken up. So, 
the first step is that of an agreem ent between the States, because these 
are all inter-State projects. Unfortunately, for example, Chhattisgarh is 
very much against the implementation of these projects. All the riparian 
States are not agreeable on the implementation of these projects. So, at 
this juncture, these cannot be considered.

Funds for irrigation Projects in Tribal Areas 
†*383. SHRI ABHAY KANT PRASAD: Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have reviewed the irrigation works in tribal 
areas; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) if not, the reasons thereof; 
 
(d) the steps taken by Government to start irrigation related 
development work in these areas; and 
(e) the amount allocated, State-wise, particularly to Jharkhand for 
development of irrigation projects in the tribal areas? 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI ARJUN CHARAN 
SETHI): (a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
Be Answered on 19.08.2003 Regarding Funds for Irrigation Projects 
in Tribal Areas. 
(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. There are 73 major and 114 medium ongoing irrigation 
projects in the X Five Year Plan wh ich are benefiting tribal areas of 16 
States. The ultimate irrigation potential of these 187 major and medium 
projects is 11.27 mha. and the achieveme nt of potential upto IX Plan is 
4.13 mha. 
(d) Special efforts have been initiated by the Government for 
development of irrigation in tribal areas according to the revised National 
Water Policy, 2002 which stipulates "special efforts should be made to 
investigate and formulate projects eith er in, or for the benefit of, areas 
inhabited by tribal or other specially disadvantaged groups such as socially 
weak, scheduled castes and scheduled tribes."

RAJYA SABHA [19 August, 2003] 
The Union Planning Commission has identified actionable points for 
development Water Sector wherein following targets had been made which 
also include projects of Tribal areas: 
1. To complete 30 major projects of Pre-fifth and Fifth Plan period 
by the States. 
2. To complete 20 major and medium projects under Fast Track of 
Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Progr amme (AIBP) for creation of 
additional 0.475 mha of irrigation potential. 
3. To create an additional 3 mha of irrigation potential through normal 
AIBP projects/schemes. 
Further, at present, out of 69 New project proposals benefiting the 
tribal areas (Under Tribal Sub Plan) there are 39 projects under different 
stages of appraisal in Central Water Commission, 29 have been techno- 
economically accepted by the Advisory Committee of the Ministry of Water 
Resources and one project has b een recommended to Planning 
Commission for investment clearance. 
(e) The allocation of funds for irrigation development in tribal areas is 
done by the concerned State Governments out of their overall allocation. 
The overall allocation for the irrigation projects including projects in the 
tribal areas for State Government of Jharkhand for the X. Five Year Plan is 
Rs. 14.632.74 crore white the agreed only for the Annual Plans 2002-03 
and 2003-04 is Rs. 2652.00 crore and Rs. 2935.85 crore respectively.

Task force on infrastructure 
2870. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state : 
(a) whether upgradation of major metro airports in India to world class 
standards was one of the mandates given by the Task Force on 
Infrastructure, set up by the Prime Minister in 1998; and 
(b) if so, the details of progress made by the Ministry of Civil Aviation 
from 1998 till date in this respect? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
(SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY): (a) Yes Sir. 
(b) The Task Force on Infrastructure on 9.12.1998 recommended that 
airports at Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore be corporatised. Based on this 
recommendation, Government of India in January, 1999 decided to 
corporatise the airports at Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata, besides 
construction of Greenfield Airport at Bangalore. Considering the 
compIexities involved in corporatisation, the Task Force on 3.6.1999 
approved the leasing route. Government of India in January, 2000 approved 
restructuring of airports of Airports Authority of India through long term 
leasing route as and when found suitable. The airports at Delhi, Mumbai 
Kolkota and Chennai were taken up for this exercise at the first instance. 
The Financial Consultant and Legal Consultant for restructuring exercise 
were appointed in March, 2000 and March, 2001 respectively. An Inter- 
Ministerial Group (IMG) was constituted to advise and monitor the entire 
exercise. The IMG met periodically to  discuss and deliberate on various 
strategic issues. Pre-lnvestment Meets were held in New Delhi and London 
in April, 2002 to formally introduce the long term lease process. The Meet 
was attended by many Airport Operators, Financial Companies etc. An 
Amendment Bill was introduced in the Parliament on 30.11.2000 for 
54 

[19 August, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
incorporating and enabling provision in the Airports Authority of India (AAI) 
Act, 1994 providing for leasing of ai rports. The Bill was referred to the 
Department Related Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and 
Culture. The Committee tabled its report on 21.11.2002. As per the 
recommendations of the Committee, a comprehensive Airports Authority 
of India (Amendment) Bill, 2003 was introduced in the Parliament.The Bill 
as passed by Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha on 9.5.2003 and 28.7.2003 
respectively. Meanwhile, the restructuring through Joint Venture route was 
also considered. The Hon'ble Finance Minister in Budget Speech 2003-04 
has inter alia announced that in addition to the existing initiatives for 
leasing of major airports, the Delhi and Mumbai airports will be taken up 
for modernisation to international standards through formation of two Joint 
Venture companies. Steps have been taken for incorporation of two 
separate companies for Delhi and Mumbai airports. The transaction 
structure is being finalised in consultation with Ministry of Finance.

SIDBI provides assistance to small scale units through indirect and 
direct finance schemes.The norms under the refinance (indirect) schemes

not exceeding 2 :1 is applicable. Re payment period and moratorium is 
fixed taking into account the debt servicing capacity of the borrowing unit 
in respect of Equipment Finance Scheme (EFS), the DER is generally

whole. As regards special schemes such as Technology Development 
and Modernisation Fund Scheme (TDMFS), the lending norms/terms are 
relatively more liberal. As regards norms/parameters, a flexible approach 
is adopted and decisions are taken based on the overall assessment of

ICICI Bank Ltd. The Interest rate a pplicable to financial assistance

commences after envisaged commissioni ng of the project and start of 
commercial operations. To ensure fiscal discipline in project 
commissioning, disbursements are usually made depending on 
achievement of specific project related milestones and only after means 
of finance is tied up. The progress of the project is monitored through

EXIM Bank offers export credit facilities to facilitate exports on deferred

(SHRI ANANDRAO VITHOBA ADSUL): (a) The Direct Taxes Enquiry 
Committee (Wanchoo Committee) in it s final Report of December, 1971

(b) Necessary legislative, fiscal  and administrative measures are 
continuously taken to prevent the ge neration and flow of black money. 
Rates of taxation have been progressi vely rationalized. Various provisions 
in the Income Tax Act; like compulsory maintenance/audit of accounts in 
appropriate cases unde r section 44AA/44AB, restrictions on cash 
transactions under section 40A(3), 269SS, 269T and penalties/prosecutions 
for punishing tax defaulters, are aimed at preventing generation and flow 
of black money. Searches and su rveys in appropriate cases are 
continuously undertaken to unearth the black money. General information 
is also gathered by the Central Info rmation Branches of the Income Tax 
Department about various financial transactions. Simplification of 
procedures for filing returns and for making payment of taxes are also 
directed towards greater compliance by the tax payers, which will be an 
anti-dote to tax evasion.

3001. DR. DASARI NARAY ANA RAO: Will the Minister of WATER

so far? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN  THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRIMATI BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The National Water Development Agency (NWDA) was established 
under the Societies Registration Act, 1862 to carry out water balance and 
feasibility studies for inter-basin water transfer proposals under Peninsular 
Component of National Perspective Plan (NPP). Subsequently, Himalayan 
Component of NPP was also included in the objectives of NWDA. 
156 

[19 August, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) The objectives of the Agency are as follows: 
To promote scientific development for optimum utilisation of water 
resources in the country. 
To carry out detailed surveys and investigations of possible 
reservoir sites and inter-connecting links in order to establish 
feasibility of the proposal of Peni nsular Rivers Development and 
Himalayan Rivers Development Components forming part of the 
National Perspective for Water Re sources Development prepared 
by the then Ministry of Irrigation (now Ministry of Water Resources) 
and Central Water Commission. 
To carry out detailed studies about the quantum of water in various 
Peninsular River systems and Himalayan River Systems which 
can be transferred to other basins/States after meeting the 
reasonable needs of the basin/States in the foreseeable future. 
To prepare feasibility report of the various components of the 
scheme relating to Peninsular Ri vers development and Himalayan 
Rivers development. 
To do all such other things the Society may consider necessary, 
incidental, supplementary or conducive to the attainment of above 
objectives. 
NWDA has completed water balance studies of basins/sub-basins

Law for water harvesting 
3005. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH: Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to enact a law not to allow building 
of individual homes or housing societies without water harvesting provisions 
throughout the country; 
(b) if so, by when an enactment is anticipated; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d) the targets fixed by Government to augment the water availability 
by reviving the traditional water system and by constructing the water 
harvesting structures throughout the country; and 
(e) the achievement made so far through both the ways? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRIMATI BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY): (a) to (c) The Union 
Government do not propose to enact a law not to allow building of individual 
homes or housing societies without water harvesting provisions throughout 
the country due to the following reasons:— 
(1) Under the Constitution of India 'Water' is a State subject and, 
thererfore, any legislation in the matter can be considered only 
by the State Legislatures. However, the Ministry of Water 
Resources has advised the Ministry of Urban Development and 
Poverty Alleviation to make roof top rain water harvesting 
mandatory. Accordingly, the Ministry of Urban Development & 
Poverty Alleviation has amended Building Bye-laws, 1983 making 
provision for water harvesting through storing of water run-off 
including rain water in all new buildings on plots of 100 square 
meters and above in Delhi mandatory. Besides, the State 
Governments of Haryana and Tamil Nadu have also issued 
amendments to municipal building bye-laws to make roof top 
rain water harvesting mandatory for specified category of 
buildings. The Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) constituted 
under Section 3 (3) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 
has also issued directions to group housing societies, institutions, 
schools, hotels, industrial establishments and farm houses 
 161 

RAJYA SABHA [19 August. 2003] 
located in 'notified areas' of South and South West districts of 
NCT Delhi, Municipal Corporation of Faridabad and Ballabgarh of 
Haryana, Municipal Corporation of  Ghaziabad in Uttar Pradesh, 
GurgaonTown and adjoining Industrial Areas of Gurgaon district 
of Haryana to adopt roof top rain water harvesting systems. The 
CGWA has also issued directions to all group housing societies 
in NCT of Delhi located in areas where ground water levels are 
more than 8 metres and are abst racting ground water to adopt 
roof top rain water harvesting system. 
(2) Water harvesting is not required in all areas of the country. There 
are areas having excess rainfall and ground water level very 
shallow. In some of the areas, even the problem of water logging 
is prevalent. 
(3) The objective can be achieved by creating mass awareness and 
organising training programmes etc. The Central Ground water 
Board (CGWB) under the Ministry of Water Resources, has 
already conducted 135 mass awareness programmes and 69 
training programmes throughout the country. 
(d) and (e) 'Water' being a State subject, it is primarily the responsibility 
of the concerned State Governments to  plan, finance and execute schemes 
to augment ground water resources. However, during the ninth Plan, the 
Central Ground water Board (CGWB) has implemented a Central Sector 
Scheme on "Studies on Recharge to Ground Water" under which 174 artificial 
recharge schemes have been approved in 27 States and U.Ts. across the 
country. All these schemes are being implemented as per targets and 115 
schemes have been completed so far. The completed schemes have 
shown positive impact in terms of rise in ground water level. However, no 
scheme to augment the water availability by reviving the traditional water 
system was undertaken under the above scheme. Further, with a view to 
augment ground water resources, the Central Government has formulated 
a Centrally Sponsored Scheme on "Ar tificial Recharge to Groundwater 
and Rain Water Harvesting" at an es timated cost of Rs.175 crore for 
implementation during the Tenth Plan. Under the Scheme, construction of 
water harvesting structures including revival of traditional water systems 
are envisaged. The scheme is at consultation stage.

Need for central assistance to regional Rural Banks 
SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, the Regional 
Rural Banks were established in 1975, essentially, for taking banking to 
the doorsteps of the rural masses particularly in areas without banking 
facilities. The Central Government is  the largest shareholder with 50 per 
cent equity share capital in RRBs, although each bank is monitored by a 
major commercial bank which holds 35 pe r cent of the share capital of the 
RRBs. Presently, there are 196 RRBs spread over 476 districts with a 
branch network of 14,350, accounting fo r 45 per cent of the total branches 
of all banks in rural India. The bulk of the loans from RRBs has been to 
priority sectors which account for 70 per cent of the total advances, 
agriculture alone accounting for 46 per cent. The involvement of RRBs in 
providing credit support to small and retail trade and other non-farm rural 
activities is better than the co-operatives and commercial banks. As the 
RRBs do not have the privilege of serving diverse base of customers as 
commercial banks, the recent decisio n of the Central Government for 
reducing the rates of interest to agriculture to 9 per cent — it is a welcoming 
development — would entail an additional burden of Rs. 600 crores, as 
against the estimated loss of income of Rs. 2,500 crores for the entire 
banking sector. This is more than the combined profit of all the RRBs, and 
unless the Central Government, which is the largest shareholder, does 
something urgently to make up for the possible loss to RRBs, there is a 
threat of their closure, denying banking to a large section of rural India. I 
rquest the Government to come out with measures to help the RRBs. 
Also, I would suggest to the Government to increase the capital base of 
the RRBs so that it can serve the farming community better. Thank you.

Demand for statehood to Pondicherry 
SHRI C. P. THIRUNAVUKKARASU (Po ndicherry): Sir, a draft Bill for 
granting statehood to Delhi had been prepared by the Union Home Ministry 
and approved by the Cabinet. The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha 
yesterday. But the long-pending demand of t he Union Territory of Pondicherry 
has not been considered by the Government. 
Sir, different Governments of Pondicherry have been requesting the 
Government of India for granting Statehood to the Union Territory of 
Pondicherry. Unanimous Resolutions have been passed in this respect. 
When the D.M.K. party was in power, a Resolution had been passed 
unanimously in the Assembly demanding Statehood for Pondicherry. All 
the Members of the legislature, the political leaders and the Members of 
Parliament met the Home Minister in this regard. But their demand has 
not been accepted. 
Sir, the elected representatives are facing administrative difficulties 
since the powers of the Chief Minister  and other Ministers are limited. All 
matters have to be referred to the Home  Ministry and the Lt. Governor for 
approval. Several proposals are either rejected, or, delayed because of 
this requirement of reference to the Home Ministry and the Lt. Governor. 
The feelings of public represent ataives have not been taken into 
consideration. 
So, the Government of India should grant Statehood and also the 
'Special Category' status to the Union Territory of Pondicherry.

House is aware that the Govern ment of Andhra Pradesh has been 
implementing the Deepam Scheme since 1999 by providing LPG 
connections to BPL women in Andhra Pradesh. So far, the Government 
has given more than 22.5 lakh LPG gas connections to BPL women in 
Andhra Pradesh. The objective of this scheme is to provide relief to the 
BPL women from drudgery in cooking with firewood, to protect the

families. The State Government is al so in the process of releasing 10

are not able to pay security deposit for getting gas connections, the 
Government of Andhra Pradesh has decided to give them a helping hand 
by paying the security deposit to the oil companies on their behalf. At 
present, the Government of Andhra Pr adesh is paying Rs. 750 as security

Urgent need for rationalisation of 
Crop Insurance Scheme 
SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA (Andhra Pradesh): Madam Deputy Chairman, 
the National Agricultural Insurance Scheme was introduced in 1999 for 
protecting the farmers against losses suffered by them due to natural 
calamities. The Government is taking a Mandal as a unit. The NAIS 
envisages, premium, for cereals, puls es, etc., at 2.5 per cent, oilseeds 
3.5 per cent and for commercial crops 6.55 per cent. To implement this, 
the Government of India set up the Agricultural Insurance Organisation. 
The AIO is adopting various methods to find out losses incurred by farmers, 
but without much help to them. For hi gh risk, indemnity is given at 60 per 
cent, for medium 80 per cent and for low-risk 90 per cent. To calculate 
loss, the AIO is putting threshold limit by taking average production of the 
last five years. Even in this, the AIO is adopting different methods for 
different crops. For example, rice or wheat taking threshold limit of last 
three years and for other crops, threshold limit is five years, and calculates 
204 

[19 August. 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
it with current year's production. If the current year's production is less 
than the average threshold limit, only then farmers get compensation. 
Secondly, groundnut was in medium-risk list in 1999, but later it included 
in high-risk list, and compensation was reduced to 60 per cent from 80 per 
cent, premium was increased to 3.5 per cent and subsidy given by the 
Government to farmers was reduced to 30 per cent from 50 per cent. This 
is only an iota of the problems. So, I request the Government of India to 
rationalise the NAIS and take a village as a unit. While calculating for 
payment of compensation, the Governm ent of India must take two years 
average crop rather than five years to decide the threshold limit. I also 
request that the activities of the AIO should be extended to Mandal level 
for effective implementation of the scheme. Thank you, Madam.
